summary: Numbered annotation markers fully implemented per spec: F selects a new `.marker` tool (toolbar `1.circle` button, tooltip "Numbered marker (F)"), click stamps sequentially numbered filled markers in the current color with contrast numeral+outline, marker diameter reuses the exact text font-size calculation so it scales identically under zoom/export, multi-digit numbers widen the marker into a capsule instead of clipping, and markers are first-class items (select/drag/delete/undo/redo/clear, export bounds, PNG editor-state round-trip, double-click inline renumbering, continue-past-max on reopen). All 246 tests pass including 17 new marker tests; pre-existing dirty work preserved untouched.
findings: All Sources/Tests files matched the provided baseline before my changes; the pre-existing dirty work (EditorImageRenderer.swift, ImageEncoding.swift, ScreenshotFinalAction.swift, workflow refactor) was already in the baseline snapshot.

Next marker number is derived as max(existing marker numbers)+1 rather than a stored counter — this automatically satisfies 'no renumbering on delete', 'preserve next number when switching tools', 'natural undo', and 'continue beyond existing max on reopen' with no state to drift.
Marker diameter equals `defaultTextFontSize` (round(38.4 / creationZoomFactor)) via `defaultMarkerDiameter`, satisfying 'scale exactly like existing text font sizing'.
Marker geometry is a capsule: `markerRect` returns a circle (w==h==diameter) for short numerals and widens with measured numeral width for multi-digit numbers — no clipping.
Numeral/outline contrast uses `NSColor.isLight` (luminance threshold) — previously private to EditorWindowController.swift, now internal for reuse by EditorImageRenderer.
Single click on an existing marker with the marker tool selects/drags it (topmost-first capsule hit test); only clicks outside any marker place a new one.

Old PNGs remain compatible: `.marker` is a purely additive `Kind` case in EditorCanvasState.Item; states without markers decode unchanged, and marker-containing states decoded by older builds simply fail decode and fall back to the flattened image.
Marker safety validation: number >= 1, finite center/color, 0 < diameter <= limits.maxFontSize; oversized/invalid markers make the state unsafe and are skipped on restore.
The 'note footer references marker numbers' requirement maps to user-written note text (NotePanelController footer is only shortcut help) — no UI added, documented in README.

decisions: Derived next-number (max+1) instead of a persisted counter — simplest correct behavior across undo/redo/clear/reopen/delete; spec wording 'continue beyond existing max' matches this exactly.
Marker stores `diameter` computed from `defaultTextFontSize` — literally shares the text sizing calculation; serialized so restored markers keep their size like text keeps fontSize.
Capsule (rounded rect, radius=h/2) that widens with numeral width rather than shrinking font inside a fixed circle — cleaner readability for multi-digit and still 'filled circle' for 1–2 digits.
Number editing reuses `EditorInlineTextView` via a shared `makeInlineEditor` factory; commit parses a positive Int, invalid input is treated like cancel (no error UI, per 'no separate prompt UI').
Cursor preview implemented with `resetCursorRects`/`addCursorRect` + `NSCursor(image:hotSpot:)` — the existing cursor infrastructure (same mechanism SelectionOverlay uses).
Placement happens on mouseDown (stamp behavior); mouseUp is a no-op for the tool.
Rejected adding marker handling to paste — region copy/cut/paste operates on flattened composites which already include markers via draw(item:); nothing marker-specific needed.

open_issues: Cursor preview badge renders at creation-zoom size (~38pt on screen, capped 16–64) since the canvas does not track live scroll magnification; after zooming in, the preview under-represents the placed size. Spec allowed 'if practical'.
Marker-tool single click on an existing marker selects/drags it rather than stacking a new marker at the same spot (chosen UX; stacking still possible by placing adjacent).

Deleting the highest-numbered marker then placing reuses that number (derived counter); deleting a middle marker never reuses or renumbers. Consistent with 'no renumbering'; flag if the intent was a monotonic counter that never reuses the max.
Editing a marker's number can create duplicate numbers by explicit user action — allowed since 'avoid duplicate numbering' was scoped to normal sequential placement.
Cursor preview not covered by tests (requires a real window); all other behaviors verified.
